meta: An angel descends on startled shepherds in a dark landscape in Jacopo Bassano's The Annunciation to the Shepherds, painted in the 1550s.
about: An angel drops out of a glowing cloud over a dark field where shepherds, cattle and a dog keep their night watch. A bearded man in pink throws up his hands, but a seated shepherd in a broad hat goes on playing his pipe. Jacopo Bassano painted it probably in the 1550s. The Duncombe family of Duncombe Park in Yorkshire probably owned it for generations, and it later passed through the hands of the collector Charles Fairfax Murray and the Florence dealer Count Contini Bonacossi. The Kress Foundation gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1939.

meta: Albrecht Dürer's 1515 iron etching of Christ praying at Gethsemane, with an angel offering a chalice from the clouds.
about: Christ kneels on a rocky hillside with a halo behind his head, and an angel in the clouds at upper right holds out a chalice. At lower left a sleeping figure lies beneath a gnarled tree. Albrecht Dürer made the print in 1515 by etching an iron plate. It was sold at a Berlin auction in 1930 and reached the collector Lessing J. Rosenwald through the Philadelphia dealer Charles Sessler. Rosenwald gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: A man reads an illustrated paper on a Paris street in Jean-Louis Forain's lithograph Rue Laffitte, made around 1892.
about: A man in profile stands absorbed in a large illustrated newspaper, and beside him a woman in a dark shawl looks out at the viewer. At the left edge a shop window frame and a small seated figure on the street cut into the scene. Jean-Louis Forain made the lithograph around 1892. Its first recorded owner was the Paris collector Alfred Beurdeley. The dealer Charles Sessler sold it in 1928 to Lessing J. Rosenwald, who gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: Hendrik Goltzius's engraving of the Adoration of the Magi, made around 1586, with a star over a stone stable.
about: A star falls bright over a stone stable where the Virgin sits beside the Christ Child and a kneeling king offers his gift. Behind them a procession of riders and camels moves along a road toward a walled town, and onlookers and children crowd in at the left. Two lines of Latin run along the lower margin. Hendrik Goltzius engraved it around 1586. The collector Lessing J. Rosenwald bought it at a Leipzig sale in 1928 and gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: Wenceslaus Hollar's 1651 etching Monk, in which a skeleton takes a robed friar by the arm.
about: A skeletal figure grips the arm of a robed monk inside an arched interior, while another skeleton lies in a panel below. Winged and female allegorical figures stand on either side with an hourglass, a scythe and a circular object. Wenceslaus Hollar etched it in 1651 after designs attributed to Abraham van Diepenbeeck and, further back, Hans Holbein the Younger. The Latin line beneath cites Psalm 106. Fritz Rumpf of Potsdam once owned it, and Lessing J. Rosenwald bought it at a Leipzig sale and gave it to the National Gallery of Art.

meta: Dragonflies, a bumble-bee and a butterfly in Wenceslaus Hollar's 1646 etching of insects.
about: Two dragonflies, a bumble-bee, a butterfly and a moth-like insect are spread across one sheet. An inscription at the upper right says that Hollar made it from the Arundel collection. Wenceslaus Hollar dated the etching 1646. Its owners began with Count Giuseppe Archinto in Milan and then Arkady Alferoff in Bonn. Rudolf Philip Goldschmidt of Berlin came next. A Leipzig sale in 1928 sent it to Lessing J. Rosenwald, who gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: Consecration of an Eagle, a niello print after Peregrino da Cesena from the early 1500s.
about: A helmeted nude man and a draped woman hold up a flaming vessel and reach toward an eagle perched on a decorated pedestal. Clouds fill the sky behind them and rocky ground lies at their feet. The print is a niello print after Peregrino da Cesena, dated about 1500 to 1525. It may once have belonged to the Durazzo collection, and the British Museum acquired it in 1873. After a Leipzig sale in 1928 it went to Lessing J. Rosenwald, and in 1943 he gave it to the National Gallery of Art.
dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 7.5 x 5.5 cm (2 15/16 x 2 3/16 in.)

meta: Georg Pencz's engraving of Queen Tomyris holding the head of Cyrus in a cloth sack.
about: A crowned nude woman holds a bearded severed head in a cloth sack, and an armored man in a plumed helmet helps her beside a tree. A second helmeted figure stands at the left edge. In the foreground lies a skull-like object. The engraving is by Georg Pencz. A collector named W. Meyer owned it in the 1800s. It was sold at a Leipzig auction in 1928 to Lessing J. Rosenwald, and he gave it to the National Gallery of Art.

meta: Rembrandt's 1633 etching The Ship of Fortune, with a robed figure on a rocky shore beside a great sailing ship.
about: A robed figure sits on a rocky shore beside a large sailing ship, and a female figure forms its prow. At left a crowd gathers under an arcade, while a rowboat full of people approaches from the right. A bust stands far back. Rembrandt van Rijn etched it in 1633. The collector Lessing J. Rosenwald bought it at a 1929 sale and lent it to Rembrandt shows in Philadelphia and Washington from 1930 to 1932. He gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.
dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 11.3 x 16.8 cm (4 7/16 x 6 5/8 in.)

meta: Rembrandt's 1651 etched portrait of Clement de Jonghe, a seated man in a wide-brimmed hat.
about: Clement de Jonghe sits turned toward us in a wide-brimmed hat, a buttoned coat and a draped cloak, with a white collar at his neck. He leans on a plain wooden chair and looks out with a calm gaze. Fine hatched lines build up the figure. Rembrandt van Rijn made the print in 1651 with etching, drypoint and burin. The Berlin collector Paul Davidsohn owned it before Lessing J. Rosenwald, who gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: Rembrandt's 1648 etching of beggars at a doorway, one hand holding out a coin.
about: A bearded man in a fur hat holds a coin out from the doorway to a family on the step. The man wears a wide-brimmed hat, the woman carries a basket and a stick, and a child rides on her back. Another young figure faces the door in the foreground. Rembrandt signed and dated the plate in the lower right corner. Among its owners was George M. La Monte of New Jersey, whose sale in 1928 preceded its purchase by Lessing J. Rosenwald.
dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 16.6 x 12.9 cm (6 9/16 x 5 1/16 in.)

meta: Rembrandt's 1653 drypoint The Three Crosses, with Christ lit by a shaft of light between the two thieves.
about: Christ hangs on the central cross in a shaft of light, with a thief crucified on each side. A dense crowd of soldiers and onlookers fills the dark foreground. Rembrandt van Rijn made the drypoint in 1653. Its owners included the London collector William Esdaile, whose sale took place in 1840, and Edward Cheney, whose sale followed in 1885. The Pasadena collector Earl Stetson Crawford sold it to Lessing J. Rosenwald, who gave it to the National Gallery of Art.
dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 39 x 45.5 cm (15 3/8 x 17 15/16 in.)

meta: Albrecht Dürer's woodcut of Christ before Caiaphas, made probably around 1509 or 1510.
about: A bound, bearded Christ stands before the seated high priest, who wears a mitre. Armoured soldiers with spears crowd in behind, and one figure raises a fist. In the foreground a dog rests beside a stone step, and a town shows past a column. Albrecht Dürer cut the design probably around 1509 or 1510. Its earlier owners were Joseph Daniel Böhm in Vienna and Robert Scholtz in Budapest. Lessing J. Rosenwald bought it from the dealer William Schab and gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: Charles Meryon's drawing of Tikao, a man of Akaroa in New Zealand, inscribed with his name and home.
about: A man with dense curly hair and a stern, frowning face looks out from an oval vignette. He wears a woven cloak fastened over one shoulder with a braided cord. Someone later wrote his name and home, Tikao of Akaroa, at the bottom. A note on the back calls it a drawing of a New Zealand chief by Meryon, from the De Salicis collection. The Glasgow collector Bernard B. MacGeorge owned it, and Lessing J. Rosenwald gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.
